title: C policy library over C++ engine
name: Authorization policy library

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code keeps C++ exceptions from escaping across its boundaries? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A C host calls authz_check with a valid handle while another thread is in the middle of PolicyEngine::reload parsing a new file. What does the check see?
choices: It blocks until parsing has finished, since reload holds the write lock for its whole duration
The previous complete rule set, because the new rules are built in a local vector and only swapped in under the lock
A partially filled rule set, since rules_ is appended to while parsing
AUTHZ_ERROR, because reload and check cannot run concurrently

questions.prompt: What does authz_check return if the policy has an allow rule and a deny rule that both match the request?
choices: AUTHZ_ALLOW, because the first matching rule wins
AUTHZ_ALLOW, because allow rules are evaluated after deny rules
AUTHZ_DENY, because a matching deny returns immediately regardless of any allow
AUTHZ_ERROR, because conflicting rules are treated as invalid

questions.prompt: Why is the message returned by authz_last_error kept in a thread_local string, and what is the caller-visible consequence?
choices: Each calling thread sees only its own most recent error, so a failure on one thread cannot overwrite the message another thread is about to read
All threads share one message, which is guarded by the engine mutex
The message is cleared automatically on the next successful call
Errors from the background reload thread are visible to the thread that started it
